title: NgRx Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the NgRx course.

entries.name: Describe an event with an action
entries.summary: An action is a named message about something that happened.

entries.name: Put a value in an action
entries.summary: props describes values carried by an action.

entries.name: Write a reducer rule
entries.summary: A reducer takes the old state and an action and returns the next state.

entries.name: Register a root store
entries.summary: provideStore connects reducer functions to root state keys.

entries.name: Read state with a selector
entries.summary: A selector is a function that chooses a useful part of state.

entries.name: Use a store value as a signal
entries.summary: Store.selectSignal gives an Angular signal for a selected value.

entries.name: Dispatch from a component
entries.summary: A component can dispatch an action in response to a user action.

entries.name: Group related action names
entries.summary: An action group keeps related event creators together.

entries.name: Keep outside work in an effect
entries.summary: An effect listens for actions and can return new actions after outside work.

entries.name: Keep a normalised list
entries.summary: A list with ids can be stored as an id array plus a lookup object.

entries.name: Try a SignalStore
entries.summary: SignalStore is another NgRx way to organise state using Angular signals.

entries.name: Test a state rule directly
entries.summary: A reducer can be tested without opening the page.
